content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing an issue that seems somewhat similar, and I'm hoping someone here can assist. I'm using a [product_name] [product_name] with a [product_name] [version_no]. I want to access digital input 1 from my program loaded in the [product_name] using the SMS command shown in the screenshot. What should the SMS command look like to activate or deactivate digital input 1? Thanks to everyone; I hope someone has advice.

Your issue is not the same; it's fundamentally different. You cannot activate or deactivate a digital input on a base module. The program can only read the current state of the digital input hardware. In other words, you are limited to viewing the digital input's status from the [product_name]; you cannot change it remotely.

Hi, and thank you for your reply. If I want to control the value of a digital input or output (I/O) in my [product_name] [version_no] by sending SMS, how should I set this up in the program using [product_name] or within the [product_name]? The SMS command I am considering is attached—please let me know if this is incorrect. Thank you for your support.
As mentioned earlier: You cannot use the [product_name] to switch a digital input (Ix) on or off. You are only able to query the status of a digital input (Ix) via the [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants aim to remotely control digital input states on a [product_name] using SMS through the [product_name], but find that only status monitoring is possible, not input activation/deactivation. There is notable confusion about what the [product_name] allows in terms of digital input interaction, suggesting that documentation or product explanations could be improved. This misunderstanding leads to disappointment as remote control functionality is not supported as some users had assumed.
